DHAKA, June 16 (Reuter) - The Bangladesh taka closed unchanged at 43.7450/7550 to the dollar in interbank trading in a quiet market, dealers said. Dealers said the taka was steady in dull trading because of lack of demand for dollars from importers. Dealers said the interbank call money rates closed at 9.0 percent to 13 percent against the previous 19-24 percent. The rates, which opend lower at 7.0-8.0 percent, gained further despite maturity of treasury bills worth 2.5 billion taka. "There is still a dearth of liquidity in the market," said one dealer.
